subject: BrightSearch top-K probe + SDK auth playbook
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>
To: Aria Johnson <aria.j@brightsearch.com>, BrightSearch SecOps <secops@brightsearch.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: BrightSearch top-K probe + SDK auth playbook

Hi Aria / SecOps team — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can unblock the PoC engineering work: 

1) Goals from our side
- Validate ranking signal improvements using Redwood's ranking API (re-rank stage) for your query set.
- Measure impact across top_k slices (1, 3, 5, 10) and report NDCG@10, MRR, Recall@K.
- Deliver an ops-ready SDK auth flow you can use in staging (short-lived service principal + SAML/OIDC path for production).

2) Architecture / integration notes we discussed
- Two integration options: client-side call to /v1/generate + server-side /v1/ranking re-ranker OR a single /v1/ranking endpoint that returns scores + chosen items. We recommend starting with the re-ranker endpoint for easier A/B with your existing ranker.
- Embeddings: use 1536-d embedding model (recommended) from Redwood for candidate retrieval; pass IDs + context to re-ranker to reduce token cost.
- Structured output: we'll enable JSON schema constraints for tool-calling downstream (we can lock shape for the re-ranker signals).

3) Auth & routing
- For PoC: we can provide a scoped service API key and a short-lived service account (service principal) for your infra team.
- Production: we recommend OIDC + per-service service accounts; SecOps asked about SAML — Redwood supports SAML via our control plane for enterprise SSO.
- Routing: canary routing by region (us-east for BrightSearch staging, fallback to hosted in us-west).

4) Evaluation plan (ask from BrightSearch)
- We need a representative query sample (ideally 5k–10k queries); please attach a CSV with query, user_intent, ground_truth_doc_ids.
- Desired KPIs: NDCG@10 primary, MRR secondary, plus latency P95 target (<= 180ms) for re-ranker path.
- We'll run top_k sweep (1,3,5,10) and produce a signal breakdown (text-match vs embedding) per slice.

Deliverables & timeline
- We propose: sample dataset by Jan 21, initial PoC results w/ metrics and plots by Jan 28, tech handoff + SDK auth docs by Feb 4.

Attachments: eval-metrics-proposal.pdf (proposal + metric definitions), brightsearch-sample-queries.csv (sample template), sdk-auth-setup.md (auth checklist).

Action items for you: please confirm the sample dataset timeframe and whether SecOps requires SAML metadata before we issue a service principal.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Thanks Vivek — this is helpful. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Sample data: we can get a 7k-query CSV to you by Jan 21. We'll include user_intent and the top 3 doc ids we consider relevant.
- SecOps: we need vendor SAML metadata + SOC2 evidence before granting an integration SA. Can you share the SAML metadata endpoint and the SOC2 upload link?

Subject: Re: BrightSearch top-K probe + SDK auth playbook

Vivek / Aria — technical follow-up from our infra side (running list):

1) API surface options
- /v1/ranking (recommended): accept query + candidate_ids + optional embeddings, returns ranked list with scores and signal breakdown. Good for server-side re-rank.
- /v1/score (alt): per-candidate scoring for tight latency budgets (calls per candidate). Higher request volume but can be parallelized.

2) Top_k sweep plan
- Run A/B with your baseline ranker vs Redwood re-ranker across these top_k values: 1, 3, 5, 10.
- Minimum sample: 5k queries for signal stability; ideal 10k. 95% CI target for NDCG differences.
- Metrics: NDCG@10 (primary), MRR@10, Recall@k (k=1,3,5), and CTR lift if available. We'll also log token cost per request to estimate unit economics.

3) Embeddings & retrieval
- Recommendation: precompute candidate embeddings (1536-d) in your pipeline and POST them as candidate_vectors to /v1/ranking to avoid extra retrieval roundtrips.
- If you cannot precompute, we can run a hybrid flow (embedding lookup -> top-100 candidate IDs -> re-rank).

4) Auth details for PoC
- For now we'll issue a scoped service API key valid for 30 days. For production please request SAML/OIDC config; SecOps will need ACS URL and SP metadata — Aria, if you share the metadata endpoint we can exchange.

5) Canary / routing
- We'll provide a canary route by header (x-rw-canary: brst-staging) so you can direct a % of traffic to Redwood re-ranker. Default fallback to current ranker on error.

Next steps (technical owners)
- BrightSearch: provide CSV sample + SecOps metadata (Aria) — due Jan 21.
- Redwood infra (Marissa): prepare PoC service key + canary route wiring — will share keys via secure Doc portal.
- Redwood evaluation (Rishi): will run the top_k sweep and produce a short report with NDCG/MRR tables by Jan 28.

(Attaching eval metrics doc + sample template in thread.)

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Experiments: baseline vs redwood_re-ranker across top_k = [1,3,5,10]; run each as paired evaluation on the same query set.
- Eval size: we'll default to 10k queries if you can provide it; otherwise we'll run on the 7k you mentioned with explicit CIs.
- Metrics: NDCG@10 (primary), MRR@10, Recall@1/3/5, mean token cost, and latency P50/P95.
- Reporting: CSV with per-query ranks + aggregated metric dashboard (GSheet link below).
